sentences.zh: 我们可能什么也得不到，除非我决定使用过度的力量和武力，坦白说，那样的话我们将势不可挡。

sentences.en: But I won't do that.
sentences.zh: 但我不会那样做。

sentences.en: But notably, he also took military action off the table.
sentences.zh: 但值得注意的是，他也排除了采取军事行动的可能性。

sentences.en: It's the United States alone that can protect this giant mass of land, this giant piece of ice, develop it and improve it.
sentences.zh: 只有美国才能保护这块巨大的陆地、这块巨大的冰体，并对其进行开发和改善。

sentences.en: So he came in and at one level he said, look, I'm not going to use force to take over this huge hunk of ice in the North Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 所以他登台后，一方面说：听着，我不会使用武力去接管北大西洋这块巨大的冰山。

sentences.en: And that's the reason I'm seeking immediate negotiations to once again discuss the acquisition of Greenland by the United States.
sentences.zh: 这也是我寻求立即展开谈判、再次讨论美国收购格陵兰岛的原因。

sentences.en: But I want to have immediate negotiations and I want you Europeans to be compliant.
sentences.zh: 但我想要立即开始谈判，而且我希望你们欧洲人顺从。

sentences.en: He said, they have a choice.
sentences.zh: 他说，他们有一个选择。

sentences.en: You can say yes and we will be very appreciative.
sentences.zh: 你们可以说“好”，我们将非常感激。

sentences.en: If we can do a deal, I'll be most appreciative.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能达成协议，我会非常感激。

sentences.en: Or you can say no.
sentences.zh: 或者你们可以说“不”。

sentences.en: Or you can say no and we will remember.
sentences.zh: 或者你们可以说“不”，而我们会记住的。

sentences.en: So it was a deeply unsettling and menacing message delivered with Trump's trademark mix of contempt and vitriol.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个极其令人不安和具有威胁性的信息，伴随着特朗普标志性的蔑视与尖刻口吻传达出来。

sentences.en: And so how is this speech received in Davos?
sentences.zh: 那么这场演讲在达沃斯是如何被解读的呢？

sentences.en: So what you see is that after a very long period of trying to flatter Trump, of trying to mollify
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的是，在经历了很长一段试图奉承特朗普、试图安抚

sentences.en: Trump, of trying to cajole Trump, European leaders are now showing a bit more of a willingness to stand up to him.
sentences.zh: 特朗普、试图哄劝特朗普的时期之后，欧洲领导人现在表现出更多站出来对抗他的意愿。

sentences.en: They're beginning to say, no way, we won't tolerate this.
sentences.zh: 他们开始说：没门，我们绝不容忍。

sentences.en: We won't accept it.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不接受。

sentences.en: And that's a really, really fascinating moment in the evolution of how foreign leaders, particularly
sentences.zh: 这是外国领导人（尤其是欧洲领导人）在应对特朗普总统方面演变历程中

sentences.en: European leaders, have dealt with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 一个非常、非常迷人的时刻。

sentences.en: NATO allies, in the words of one former American diplomat, had gone through five stages of grief with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 用一位前美国外交官的话说，北约盟友已经经历了对特朗普总统的五个悲伤阶段。

sentences.en: It began with denial right after he got back into the White House.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于他重返白宫后的否认阶段。

sentences.en: It transitioned very quickly to anger, perhaps after that terrible meeting that Trump had with Vladimir Zelensky of Ukraine, shifted to bargaining, continued into depression, and
sentences.zh: 局势很快转变为愤怒，或许在特朗普与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基进行那次可怕的会晤之后，情绪转为讨价还价，接着陷入沮丧，并

sentences.en: has finally arrived at something approaching acceptance.
sentences.zh: 最终迎来了某种接近接受的状态。

sentences.en: And can you explain, Mark, why this is the thing that has prompted that change?
sentences.zh: 马克，你能解释一下，为什么这件事会成为促成这种转变的原因吗？

sentences.en: Why is this the moment that leaders in Europe are turning away from, as you said, the strategy of kind of, you know, placating Trump to now going much harder at him?
sentences.zh: 为什么在这个时刻，正如你所说，欧洲领导人开始不再采取那种安抚特朗普的策略，转而对采取更强硬的对抗姿态？

sentences.en: I think what it has to do with is the fact that these leaders, who felt during the period of time
sentences.zh: 我认为这与这样一个事实有关：这些领导人曾在一段时间内感到

sentences.en: that they were negotiating with President Trump over tariffs, that there was a deal to be done,
sentences.zh: 在与特朗普总统就关税问题进行谈判时，他们觉得双方是有达成协议的可能的，

sentences.en: that they could do business with him, that they could get some of the damage limited.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己可以与他做生意，可以把一些损失降到最低。

sentences.en: I think in this case, they view this as far more fundamental, far more existential.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这次事件中，他们认为这要根本得多，也更具有生死攸关的意义。

sentences.en: And it's one in which they felt they had to take a stand.
sentences.zh: 这是一个他们觉得必须表明立场的事件。

sentences.en: They had to draw a line.
sentences.zh: 他们必须划定底线。

sentences.en: This is not open to negotiation.
sentences.zh: 这没有谈判的余地。

sentences.en: This is a moment where you have to stand up for your values.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你必须挺身而出捍卫自身价值观的时刻。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块拼字游戏《Connections》的创作者之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特性。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到那些声音的主人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: Okay, Mark.
sentences.zh: 好的，马克。

sentences.en: So you just said that America's allies essentially came to the view that this Greenland issue was much bigger than just Greenland itself.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才提到，美国的盟友们基本上形成了一种看法，即格陵兰岛的问题远比格陵兰岛本身要宏大得多。

sentences.en: They came to see this as something you described as existential.
sentences.zh: 他们开始将这视为你所描述的关乎生死存亡的事情。

sentences.en: Just describe, if you can, why they view these threats as such a fundamental risk.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，请描述一下，为什么他们会将这些威胁视为如此根本的风险？

sentences.en: Because Europe really views the system of international law, of a rules-based order,
sentences.zh: 因为欧洲确实将国际法体系以及基于规则的秩序

sentences.en: as central to its existence, to its economic prosperity, and frankly, to Western liberal democracy.
sentences.zh: 视为其生存、经济繁荣，乃至坦率地说，西方自由民主的核心。

sentences.en: All of that is put at risk by having a sudden rupture, a shattering of this rules-based order.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都因这种基于规则的秩序发生突然破裂和粉碎而面临风险。

sentences.en: And so what you saw in Davos was a series of leaders stepping up on the dais to sort of warn about the costs of this
sentences.zh: 所以在达沃斯，你看到一系列领导人走上讲台，警告这样做的代价，

sentences.en: and to begin to talk about what they need to do to respond to it.
sentences.zh: 并开始讨论他们需要采取什么行动来应对。

sentences.en: So you had President Macron of France get up and talk about how we prefer partners to bullies.
sentences.zh: 法国总统马克龙站出来谈论我们更喜欢合作伙伴而非霸凌者。

sentences.en: And most extraordinarily, you had Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada deliver, I think, what's going to be remembered for years as an extremely significant speech.
sentences.zh: 最非同寻常的是，加拿大总理马克·卡尼发表了我认为未来多年都将被铭记的、极具分量的一场演讲。

sentences.en: It seems that every day we're reminded that we live in an era of great power rivalry.
sentences.zh: 似乎每天都在提醒我们，我们生活在一个大国竞争的时代。

sentences.en: In which he described what's at stake in the loss of the international order.
sentences.zh: 他在演讲中描述了失去国际秩序所面临的利害关系。

sentences.en: For decades, countries like Canada prospered under what we called the rules-based international order.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，像加拿大这样的国家在我们所称的基于规则的国际秩序下走向繁荣。

sentences.en: And he went back into history and described how this order was set up, who it benefited, of course, principally the United States.
sentences.zh: 他回顾历史，描述了这一秩序是如何建立的，它让谁受益，当然，主要还是美国。

sentences.en: And American hegemony in particular helped provide public goods, open sea lanes, a stable financial system.
sentences.zh: 尤其是美国霸权帮助提供了公共产品、开放的海上航线以及稳定的金融系统。

sentences.en: How there were elements of dishonesty and hypocrisy to that system.
sentences.zh: 同时也存在该系统不诚实和虚伪的成分。

sentences.en: We knew the story of the international rules-based order was partially false.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，基于规则的国际秩序这个故事有一部分是虚假的。

sentences.en: That the strongest would exempt themselves when convenient.
sentences.zh: 也就是最强大的国家在方便时会将自己豁免在外。

sentences.en: Which nevertheless, everybody went along with because not only did the United States benefit, but the smaller and middle powers did too.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，大家还是随波逐流，因为不仅美国从中受益，中小国家也同样受益。

sentences.en: Both through the economic ties that were generated by it, and crucially, the protection it afforded to the weaker states.
sentences.zh: 这既得益于由此产生的经济联系，更关键的是得益于它为弱小国家提供的保护。

sentences.en: And essentially what Mark Carney said is...
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，马克·卡尼所说的是……

sentences.en: Let me be direct.
sentences.zh: 容我直言。

sentences.en: We are in the midst of a rupture, not a transition.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于一个断裂期，而不是过渡期。

sentences.en: That system is over.
sentences.zh: 那个系统已经结束了。

sentences.en: That bargain no longer exists between the great powers and the middle powers.
sentences.zh: 大国与中小国家之间的这种交易已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: You cannot live within the lie of mutual benefit through integration when integration becomes the source of your subordination.
sentences.zh: 当一体化成为你被从属的根源时，你就不能再生活在通过一体化实现互利共赢的谎言之中了。

sentences.en: We now live in an openly predatory world.
sentences.zh: 我们现在生活在一个公开掠夺的世界里。

sentences.en: The powerful have their power.
sentences.zh: 强权者拥有他们的力量。

sentences.en: But we have something too.
sentences.zh: 但我们也有我们的东西。

sentences.en: The capacity to stop pretending.
sentences.zh: 那就是停止假装的能力。

sentences.en: And for countries like Canada, like other European countries, to survive in that world, they're going to need to be much more pragmatic, to some extent less values-driven,
sentences.zh: 对于加拿大以及其他欧洲国家来说，要想在那个世界中生存，他们需要变得更加务实，在某种程度上减少价值观驱动，

sentences.en: willing to cut deals with a greater number of actors, including China.
sentences.zh: 愿意与更多的行为体达成交易，包括中国。

sentences.en: That is Canada's path.
sentences.zh: 这就是加拿大的道路。

sentences.en: We choose it openly and confidently, and it is a path wide open to any country willing to take it with us.
sentences.zh: 我们公开而自信地选择它，这是一条向任何愿意与我们同行国家敞开的宽广道路。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: And so if Donald Trump, in his characteristically visceral way, was laying out the threat,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果说唐纳德·特朗普以其极具个人风格的直观方式提出了威胁，

sentences.en: Mark Carney was supplying in a deeply articulate way the response.
sentences.zh: 那么马克·卡尼则以深刻清晰的方式给出了应对之策。

sentences.en: And the speech by Carney was especially striking.
sentences.zh: 卡尼的演讲尤为引人注目。

sentences.en: Worth noting, it got a standing ovation.
sentences.zh: 值得一提的是，它赢得了全场起立鼓掌。

sentences.en: But for the purposes of understanding this moment, essentially what Carney is saying is that this fiction of a rules-based world order is now over.
sentences.zh: 但为了理解当前的时刻，卡尼本质上是在说，基于规则的世界秩序这种虚构已经结束了。

sentences.en: The mask is off.
sentences.zh: 面具已经摘下。

sentences.en: The hegemon that we've all been relying on, the United States, is now essentially turning against us.
sentences.zh: 我们一直依赖的霸权国家——美国，现在本质上正在调转枪头对付我们。

sentences.en: And so my question, Mark, is in standing up to that hegemon, what cards does the rest of NATO actually have to play?
sentences.zh: 所以我的问题是，马克，在挺身对抗这个霸权时，北约其他成员国实际上还有什么筹码可以打？

sentences.en: Well, this is, of course, the heart of the matter.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这当然是问题的核心所在。

sentences.en: And on one level, you have to say they don't have a lot of cards.
sentences.zh: 从某种层面上讲，你必须承认他们并没有多少筹码。

sentences.en: Were the United States to launch an all-out military assault on Greenland, there is a 0% chance that Germany, France, the United Kingdom, and Denmark
sentences.zh: 如果美国对格陵兰岛发动全面军事进攻，德国、法国、英国和丹麦有零的概率

sentences.en: are going to go to war with the United States.
sentences.zh: 会与美国开战。

sentences.en: Now, remember, of course, President Trump appeared to rule that out.
sentences.zh: 现在，记住，当然特朗普总统似乎已经排除了这种可能性。

sentences.en: But, you know, with regard to other threats, notably the threat in Ukraine, the threat from Russia, you're already beginning to see the outlines of that kind of response.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，关于其他威胁，特别是乌克兰的威胁、来自俄罗斯的威胁，你已经开始看到这种回应的轮廓。

sentences.en: Germany has joined France and the UK in building what they call a coalition of the willing, a proposal to send tens of thousands of troops to Ukraine or around Ukraine
sentences.zh: 德国已经加入法国和英国的行列，建立他们所谓的“愿意者联盟”，这是一项向乌克兰或乌克兰周边派遣数万名部队的提议，

sentences.en: to help secure the country in the event of a ceasefire with Russia.
sentences.zh: 以便在与俄罗斯停火的情况下帮助保障该国的安全。

sentences.en: You could see a series of smaller alliances between Baltic countries or between Mediterranean countries.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到巴罗海三国之间或地中海国家之间出现一系列较小的联盟。

sentences.en: So it doesn't have the overarching feel of the NATO alliance, but there are these more piecemeal arrangements that countries can make with each other
sentences.zh: 所以它没有北约联盟那种总体全局的感觉，但这些是国家之间可以建立的更加零散的安排，

sentences.en: and I think this is what Carney is talking about.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是卡尼在谈论的内容。

sentences.en: It's messier, it's riskier, it's more expensive, but in this predatory world, it may be the best that these middle powers can hope for.
sentences.zh: 它更混乱、风险更高、成本也更高，但在这样一个弱肉强食的世界里，这可能是这些中小国家所能期望的最好结果了。

sentences.en: Basically, you're saying that one strategy would be for these NATO countries to get themselves in a position to eventually rely a lot less on the United States
sentences.zh: 基本上，你是说其中一种战略是让这些北约国家做好准备，最终大大减少对美国的依赖

sentences.en: when it comes to security, especially with regard to the threat from Russia.
sentences.zh: 在涉及安全问题时，特别是面对来自俄罗斯的威胁时。

sentences.en: Obviously, that would be a long-term strategy.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这将是一项长期战略。

sentences.en: That would take time to play out.
sentences.zh: 这需要时间来发挥作用。

sentences.en: Generations.
sentences.zh: 需要几代人的时间。

sentences.en: Europe, because it was under this American security umbrella since the end of World War II, would have to take literally decades to build up an independent security force
sentences.zh: 由于欧洲自二战结束以来一直处于这个美国安全保护伞之下，它将需要字面意义上的数十年时间来建立一个独立的、

sentences.en: that had no reliance or little reliance on the United States.
sentences.zh: 对美国没有依赖或只有很少依赖的安全力量。

sentences.en: And that would involve extremely difficult decisions by governments about how to spend public resources.
sentences.zh: 这将涉及各国政府关于如何支办公共资源的极其艰难的决定。

sentences.en: Remember, these are countries that are used to generous social welfare programs, welfare programs that are funded by governments that historically did not have to spend
sentences.zh: 请记住，这些国家习惯了慷慨的社会福利项目，这些福利项目是由那些历史上一向不需要在国防和军事上像美国那样投入巨资的政府所资助的。

sentences.en: as much on defense and the military as the United States did.
sentences.zh: 这还只是一个层面的问题。

sentences.en: So that's on one level.
sentences.zh: 在经济层面上，这些国家至少在理论上确实拥有一些筹码。

sentences.en: On the economic level, it is true that these countries, at least in theory, do have some leverage.
sentences.zh: 例如，在贸易方面，欧盟可以对包括美国在内的其他国家实施所谓的反胁迫措施。

sentences.en: On the trade front, for example, the European Union can impose what they call anti-coercion measures against other countries, including the United States.
sentences.zh: 这就是俗称的“巴祖卡”武器。

sentences.en: This is something that's colloquially known as the bazooka.
sentences.zh: 那么“巴祖卡”到底是什么？

sentences.en: And what is the bazooka exactly?
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以巴祖卡基本上是欧洲人可以对他们认为采取了不公平贸易做法的其他国家实施的一系列极其严厉的措施。

sentences.en: Well, so bazooka is basically a series of very draconian measures that the Europeans can impose on another country that they think has hit them with unfair trade practices.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对在欧洲做生意的许多美国公司和投资者来说将是非常痛苦的。

sentences.en: And of course, that would be very painful for the many American companies and investors that do business in Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种形式的筹码。

sentences.en: So that is a form of leverage.
sentences.zh: 但欧盟内部对于是否使用这样的措施似乎远未达成一致。

sentences.en: But there seems to be well short of unanimity within the European Union about using measures like that.
sentences.zh: 这就触及了欧洲长期存在的顽疾，那就是在面对像美国这样强大的对手时，很难在任何这些立场周围达成足够的团结，使其真正发挥效力。

sentences.en: And that goes to what is the perennial problem with Europe, which is achieving enough unity around any of these positions to make them truly effective when you're facing, you know,
sentences.zh: 我猜这也是为什么很难在动用你所说的这种经济“巴祖卡”上达成共识的部分原因，因为这存在风险。

sentences.en: a major adversary like the United States.
sentences.zh: 这里有着巨大的风险。

sentences.en: And I presume also part of the reason it's hard to get on the same page about using what you call this economic bazooka is that there's a risk to it.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，特朗普表示他不会实施他曾威胁要征收的额外新关税。

sentences.en: There's a huge risk to it.
sentences.zh: 但他一直在关税问题上反复无常。

sentences.en: At this moment, Trump is saying he's not going to impose the additional new tariffs he had threatened.
